newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's first investment fund value up 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's first investment fund value up 30 percent.

text.p: Kaptol Proinvest, Croatia's only investment fund, said on Thursday the value of its portfolio had increased almost 30 percent in seven months since opening.
Proinvest was set up and fully-owned by the small private Kaptol Banka. It was the first, and so far the only, mutual fund operating on the Croatian financial market.
Its shares grew steadily to 129.57 kuna on Thursday from their 100 kuna nominal value on January 8, when it started operating, said Lidija Maricic, spokeswoman for Kaptol Banka.

The bank charges a five-percent commission to enter the fund. The open-type fund has so far attracted 3.7 million kuna but is still well short of its projection of 20 million kuna by the end of the year.
"We are happy with the interest given the fact that people know very little about this sort of investing," Maricic told Reuters.

The fund is conservatively managed, as some 47 percent of its portfolio is invested in the Croatian money market, 27 percent in government bonds and less than 17 percent in the more volatile stock market.
Kaptol Banka is managed and partly-owned by Dejan Kosutic, a grandson of Croatia's powerful President Franjo Tudjman. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, + 385-1-4557075
